claim: Let \(T=\omega^{<\omega}\) be ordered by extension, and let \(\mathfrak{o}\) and \(\bar{\mathfrak{o}}\) be the least sizes of maximal almost-disjoint families of infinite off-branch sets and infinite antichains, respectively. If \(\mathcal O\) is a maximal off-branch family in which every member has finite chain height (with no uniform height bound required), then there is a maximal almost-disjoint family \(\mathcal B\) of infinite antichains with \(|\mathcal B|\le|\mathcal O|\). Consequently, if \(\mathfrak{o}<\bar{\mathfrak{o}}\), every \(\mathfrak{o}\)-sized maximal off-branch family contains a member of unbounded finite chain height.

correctness.rationale: For each member A of finite height, longest-chain rank is finite and strictly increases along proper extensions, so each rank level is an antichain. The finite rank partition preserves an infinite intersection with any antichain C. Subsets preserve pairwise finite intersections, and the finite number of levels per member gives |B| <= |O| times aleph_0 = |O|.
